thread:
mira: heads-up -- onboarding zephyrus14b v2 (int4) is tripping transient OOMs during warmup when traffic ramps. Repro steps and logs below. tagging @sam @leo for quick triage.

sam: is this just during canary ramp or reproducible in stress tests?

mira: reproducible in both. small local stress: 12 concurrency, 8 short prompts causes OOM on some GPUs within ~20s. Default config looks dangerous. Logs: 
```
2026-03-20T18:12:03Z ERROR worker-3 OOM allocate 1.2GiB for kv-cache
2026-03-20T18:12:03Z WARN serve falling back to slow-path, request dropped
```

leo: what's current runtime config?

mira: current model config: {"batch_size":48, "batch_max_tokens":1200, "max_new_tokens":256, "slow_start_ratio":0.0, "kv_eviction":"lru"}

jess: quick theory: high max_new_tokens + large batch causes big KV allocations and fragmentation during warm allocation. Two levers: reduce default max_new_tokens and add allocation cushion + slow start.

ryan: agree. For other 14b int4s we added memory_cushion_mb and switched to trim-on-alloc eviction to reduce fragmentation peaks. Also microbatch for warmup. Example: memory_cushion_mb=512, kv_eviction="trim_on_alloc", microbatch_threshold=4.

mira: tried a canary patch with conservative defaults: {"batch_size":32, "batch_max_tokens":900, "max_new_tokens":128, "slow_start_ratio":0.2, "microbatch_threshold":4, "memory_cushion_mb":512, "kv_eviction":"trim_on_alloc"}

sam: results?

mira: 2-hour canary, 0 OOMs across 8 canary hosts. Tail latency for new workers increased ~15% for first ~30s then stabilizes. Throughput steady.

leo: any eval impact from dropping max_new_tokens to 128?

mira: ran standard evals (safety + short/med length gen). Mostly identical. We scheduled a dedicated long-form generation eval (24h) to catch regressions.

jess: propose route-level overrides: default 128 but keep 256 for routes marked long-form. Redwood routing can select config per-route. That keeps UX for known long-gen endpoints.

ryan: also suggest prefetch_headroom=2 during warmups so a tiny KV prefix is materialized ahead of the full allocation; that lowered coldstart spikes on cerulean16b. Combine with slow_start_ratio to ramp concurrency.

mira: implemented route override prototype and enabled prefetch_headroom=2 in canary. Ops-bot started deploy-canary cfg id cfg-zi-331 to hosts host-54..host-61.

ops-bot: deploy-canary started for zephyrus14b:v2 cfg-zi-331 -> host-54, host-55, host-56, host-57, host-58, host-59, host-60, host-61

sam: action items: 1) mira: finalize canary config and keep default=128 + route override for long-gen (done?) 2) sam: run long-gen eval and post diffs 3) ryan: add kv-churn and fragmentation percentiles to console for warmup window and add alert if fragmentation >40%

jess: minor note: consider setting reserve_tokens=128 on long-form routes instead of increasing max_new_tokens globally; reserve_tokens avoids evicting other requests' KV slices.

mira: good idea. I will run a quick AB: default128 vs default128+reserve_tokens on long routes. Also will try memory_cushion variants (512 vs 768) and report latencies + OOM/no-oom outcome.

leo: if long-gen eval shows drop in quality, we can add a post-generation rehydrate step (one-off worker with higher reservation) or transparently route to dedicated capacity for long-form jobs.

ryan: for observability add a short-lived metric during rollout: warmup_kv_evictions_per_min and kv_trim_fail_rate. We'll surface 95/99 pctl fragmentation over first 60s.

mira: thanks all. Will post perf numbers and eval diffs tomorrow AM. For now patch is in canary and looks stable. :thumbsup:
